story.headline: More than bragging rights at stake when No. 3 Utah hosts No. 7 BYU in Big 12, state rivalry clash
paragraphs: For the first time ever, BYU and Utah will face each other as Top 10 teams.

This year’s edition of the Holy War offers bigger stakes than simple bragging rights. When the No. 3 Utes host the No. 7 Cougars on Saturday, the outcome could go a long way to determining the eventual Big 12 champion and forecast which teams from the league can secure a College Football Playoff bid in December.

“No one deserves this more than the state of Utah to be able to have a game like this,” Utah quarterback Devon Dampier said. “I feel like our rivalry is a little slept on sometimes from the outside world, but our rival games are the best.”

Utah (8-0, 5-0 Big 12, No. 3 CFP) is one of three unbeaten FBS teams and the owner of the nation’s longest winning streak at 14 games. The Utes sit a full game ahead of both BYU and Texas Tech in the Big 12 standings.

story.headline: UCLA, still unbeaten and ranked No. 5, hits the road to face a Minnesota team in full big-game mode
paragraphs: Field storms became the norm last month at Minnesota, where upsets fervently returned two long-absent rivalry trophies to campus.
The unbeaten UCLA Bruins and their ball-hawking defense are coming this week to try to keep Gophers fans safely in the stands.

Fifth in the latest Associated Press poll and eighth in the first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings, UCLA entered the final third of the schedule as one of three FBS teams left without a loss in this remarkable turnaround in coach Bob Chesney's debut.

After leading James Madison to a playoff berth in just the program's fourth year at the NCAA's top level, Chesney has confidently and energetically taken his acumen from one coast to the other with a sizeable contingent of assistants and players joining him on the journey. But for all they've done to revive the Rose Bowl during this storybook regular season, the hardest part for the Bruins remains.

story.headline: No. 9 Alabama and No. 15 LSU close out their annual November matchups with yet another big game

“November, meaningful games, that’s — I don't mean arrogantly — that’s what we’ve been used to for a lot of years now,” Kiffin said, referring to both LSU and his own coaching experience at other programs.

“We should be even in better position,” Kiffin continued, referring to narrow road losses to No. 12 Mississippi and No. 8 Kentucky. “Less margin for error than we would have. So, we’ve got to be on everything and we’ve got to make sure that we perform really well against a really good team that’s coached really well that has really good players.”

story.headline: Without star WR Malachi Toney, No. 1 Miami visits No. 4 Notre Dame on Saturday
paragraphs: For Notre Dame, this season comes with a mantra of “leave no doubt.”

A game that has been hyped for months — No. 1 Miami at No. 4 Notre Dame — awaits Saturday night, a rematch from last season's contest that got the Hurricanes into the College Football Playoff and kept the Fighting Irish out. But the Hurricanes lost top receiver Malachi Toney this week to an ankle injury, a huge blow to a Miami team facing a ranked opponent for the first time this season.

“They’ve got great players,” Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman said Thursday. “I’m not saying one person’s going to replace Malachi Toney, but they have a lot of great players on their team and they’re going to find ways to get their best players on the field.”

For both sides, the stakes are enormous. Miami (8-0, No. 1 CFP) could send a serious message if it finds a way to win at Notre Dame Stadium without Toney — who had been a Heisman Trophy favorite entering the week, then had surgery on Thursday with hopes of returning this season. Notre Dame (7-1, No. 11 CFP) knows its margin of error is now slim, after being lower than many thought in the initial playoff rankings.
